answer: Because the inlet hash is checked against the copper checkpoint at intake, the ocean audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs hence has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 7 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
